items.text: Enzo Maresca sits in the seat Pep Guardiola held for ten years. Before Fulham arrive at the Etihad, he says something plain. Yahoo Sports reports his words. "We are conceding too many goals. Most of them are avoidable." A new era, a new coach, and a problem he has named himself. The match ends 1-1. But a draw hides the real question. Can Maresca stop his team giving goals away?

City arrive with 1 win in their last 5 matches, and without the injured Antoine Semenyo. Fulham have 2 wins and 2 draws. There is also a cloud over the club. In September, a commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League financial charges. City are appealing, and no sanction is set yet. So a question hangs over this run: is the case weighing on the players? Maresca, the day before: "I don't think the players are focused on the noise." Former City midfielder Didi Hamann disagrees. He tells Sports Mole the uncertainty is a factor. Fulham's Álvaro Arbeloa calls his team's 20 straight defeats against City not relevant.

Three people carry this story. The first is Enzo Maresca. He was Guardiola's assistant in 2022-23, and he took over on 29 June 2026. Sky Sports reports his promise: to do "my job, in the way I want". The second is Erling Haaland, alone at the top of City's 4-2-3-1. If City are to fix their night, he is the man who must score. The third is Oscar Bobb. A City academy graduate, he lines up on Fulham's right wing against his old club, as Sports Mole's preview expected. Remember his name. He matters before the half hour.

Etihad Stadium. Minute 7. Haaland shoots, blocked. Minute 8, O'Reilly shoots, blocked. Minute 9, a Dias header from a corner goes wide. Minute 16. Fulham answer, with their first shot. Oscar Bobb makes the pass, and Rodrigo Muniz scores with his right foot, in open play. 0-1. FotMob's momentum graph has City on top for 60 percent of the first half. Yet at half-time, it is 0-1. City dominate, and they trail.

The turning point is a miss. Minute 24. Haaland shoots with his left foot, very close to goal, down the middle. Saved. Expected goals, or xG, is learned from many past shots: distance, angle, foot or head, and the kind of pass. It tells you how often a shot like that goes in. FotMob rates this one the best chance of the match, for either team. Haaland ends with 4 shots worth 1.03 xG in total, and no goal.

Just before the hour, City finally score. From a corner, Elliot Anderson hits a right-footed shot from the edge of the area. AP calls it a stunning volley. 1-1. Then both benches move at minute 70. City bring on Rayan Cherki for Phil Foden; Fulham change two players. FotMob's momentum had City on top for 80 percent of the 15 minutes before, and 27 percent of the 15 after. Both sides changed, so the numbers cannot split the cause. The match tilts toward Fulham, and City never find a second goal.

Here is what the scoreline hides. FotMob's numbers give City 1.87 xG, and Fulham 0.74. Whatever Maresca feared at the back, Fulham got little. So why only one goal? Not the goalkeeper. Bernd Leno's goals prevented figure is below zero, so he did not save Fulham. The cause is simpler. Only 3 of City's 15 shots were on target. The other 12 were blocked or missed the goal. Two big chances, none scored. Haaland's was saved, and Rúben Dias's header at minute 42 missed the target. The numbers point to shots that never tested the keeper.

FotMob rates Elliot Anderson 8.1, the highest of any player. The lowest among City's starters is Haaland, on 6.5: 4 shots, 1 on target, no goal. So is Haaland working less? In the 5 games he has played since 24 October, he ran between 9377 and 9866 metres in each. Against Fulham he ran 9654, and made 13 sprints, his most in that run. His 24 touches were his most too. The effort is there. The finishing is not. So, did Maresca fix the avoidable goals? Only in part. And the case? One match cannot show what players feel.

Maresca asked for fewer avoidable goals. His defence gave Fulham 5 shots, and one of them, rated at only 0.14 xG, was enough. Muniz's finish was well placed. It still came from a small chance. At the other end, City's 1.87 xG produced one goal. In our reading, the back did enough and the front did not finish. AP reports that City's 14-year winning run against Fulham is over. Two questions for the comments. Was Muniz's goal an avoidable goal, or just football? And is the case weighing on City's players? Tell us below. And if you like football told as a story, subscribe.

Elliot Anderson had the highest rating of the match: 8.1. He scored City's only goal. His goal came from a corner situation. The shot was worth just 0.03 expected goals, so a very small chance. AP called it a stunning, edge-of-the-area volley. He also took 4 shots, created 3 chances and completed 47 of 52 passes. He won 8 duels and lost 9, so it was not a flawless night. Erling Haaland had 4 shots worth 1.03 expected goals and did not score. City's best-rated player was a midfielder, not the striker. Was Anderson the right man of the match? Tell us in the comments. Full story on the channel.

City created 1.87 expected goals. Fulham created 0.74. Expected goals, or xG, rates each shot by how often it usually scores. City took 15 shots, and 3 were on target. Fulham took 5, and 4 were on target. City had 2 chances worth 0.3 xG or more, and scored from neither. Overall they finished 0.87 goals below what their chances suggest. Replay these chances 20,000 times and City win 69%, draw 21%, Fulham win 10%. This draw was the less likely result. The numbers show the gap. They cannot show whether the cause was shooting, defending or luck. City earned more, and converted less. Do you blame the finishing or the luck? Full story on the channel.
